intro: The forty-sixth screen read 106 pictures, the set's 21 and 85 probes, with fourteen readers and five scorers: 1,102 of 1,144 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. **Every template passes the legibility gate, all 64, and every person has a new head with a jaw and a chin.** The head was chosen blind: four shapes were built in Blender, ranked on one sheet and then read two at a time, and the round jaw won both of its pairings in both orders. `rain_coming`, which failed v0.48's gate, reads 1.00 in five pictures with v0.48's drawing, a new gesture having read worse on the bench. The ice cream, now at the mouth, is eaten or licked in 13 of its 14 pictures, and the moustache is named again, in 13 of its wearer's 22. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. Three things stand against the gate. The set's score fell to 0.967 from 0.993, all of it on the setting: nine of its ten items under full marks are the clouds or the sun, left out by a reader, and 41 of the 42 across the screen are the clouds, a tree or the sun, left out by seven readers. The jaw has not made grown figures read as grown: four of them are called a girl or a boy first in 20 of their 89 pictures, for 11 of 81 in v0.48, and that heads the oddities for v0.50. And many full marks still carry a hedge: on the strict count 54 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.48's 55.
design:
## Design tests

The cast of builder 0.49.0 and revision 46's rules were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v049.md`, eight pictures, one fresh reader each). The bench had read the heads in rows and in pairs and the figures alone; this was the first time a reader had them at a picture's size. Between them the eight forced sets hold nine of the ten people, the storm watcher twice, the ice cream four times and the goat on its rope. Seven placed on their first seed and one on its twelfth. Two forced sets were changed before any picture of theirs existed, because the first could not be cast or placed; no picture was built again, before a reading or after one.

Every forced event was read, twenty-four of twenty-four. That is a count of what a reader wrote about a picture built to show the event; it is not the screen, where a scorer who has not seen the picture marks each item against the description. What the readers wrote:
- **The storm watcher,** twice, v0.48's pointer: "points up at the sky, as if pointing out the dark clouds or warning that rain is coming." Both readers went on to the rain, and both hedged what the finger is on: "She is most likely pointing at the storm clouds, to warn about rain, but she could also be pointing at the fence or gate."
- **The ice cream,** four times: eaten in two with no hedge, "walks along eating a pink ice-cream cone", and hedged in two, "is licking or holding a pink ice-cream cone".
- **The walker and the box:** "A cardboard box sits on the pavement right in front of her, so she looks about to trip over it."
- **The goat's rope:** "its lead hangs down to a small stake or peg in the ground", and still slight at a picture's size: "it is a thin line and the peg is small, so it could be missed or read as a stick".
- **The dog begging:** "looking up at the boy as if begging for the ice cream".

What the tests showed first, and the screen then counted: the grown figures are still read young. The four that v0.48's screen had called young appear nine times in the eight pictures and are called by a young name first in four: "a girl with a dark ponytail, purple top and teal trousers"; "a boy in a red shirt and blue trousers". Where the bearded man stands in front, his beard is the first thing said of him: "a man with dark skin and a beard". The eight were built while the revision's edge rule still applied to every figure; the rule decides where a figure may stand and draws nothing, so the readings are kept as readings of the cast. Nothing was mended after the readings; each remark went to the screen as it stood.
screen:
Across all 106 pictures 1,102 of 1,144 scored items had full marks, and none was misread (v0.48: 939 of 971, none). Of the 42 under full marks:
- forty-one are setting items that seven readers left out, twenty-nine the clouds, eleven a tree and one the sun, all zeros (v0.48 had twenty-three, from two readers). Two readers left the clouds out of all eight of their pictures;
- one is the lost balloon's inference, a half mark: "The red balloon may belong to the girl (she let go) or to someone else; she seems to be reaching for it."

The set's headline is all items 0.967 (0.993 in v0.48). Of its 284 items ten are under full marks: the clouds in eight pictures and the sun in one, which their readers left out (things 0.917, from 0.990), and half of the lost balloon's inference (inferences 0.985, as in v0.48). Its actions and its contradictions lost nothing (1.00 each), and none of its items was misread. The fall is a reader's habit and not a drawing's fault: the same clouds are named by the other readers of the same settings. A person tested will leave them out too, so the pilot's scoring has to say whether setting items count.

**After the screen.** Nothing was changed: no probe or isomorph was swapped and no picture was read again. A probe swapped for one that looks better to its builder is selection, and a second reading of an unchanged picture is a second roll of the dice.

**The rain.** `rain_coming` failed v0.48's gate when one reader named the clouds and the pointer and did not go on to the rain. v0.49 tried a new gesture, a watcher with a hand held out, palm up, for the first drop, and it read worse on the bench than the pointer it was to replace: of four readers one had the rain first, two had it as one of two readings, and one had the watcher "looking and pointing toward the right, roughly at a small café table with two chairs". Both readers of the pointer on the same seeds went on to the rain. So the pointer stays, in five probe pictures for three, and the rain is said in all five: "It looks as if it is about to rain."; "pointing up at the dark clouds as though rain is coming". That is a pass on more pictures and other readers, not a mended visual.

**The ice cream.** v0.48's cone stopped short of the mouth, and two walkers were "just holding the cone up". The scoop is at the mouth now and the head tips to it: eaten or licked in 13 of 14 pictures, "walks along the path eating a pink ice-cream cone", and in the fourteenth a running child is "holding a pink ice-cream cone up near his face". Two of its fourteen full marks are a call about the eating, where v0.48 had two half marks and eight calls in twenty.

**The cast in the descriptions.** No description of the 106 has the word jaw or chin or writes of a head's shape, which is weak evidence, as it was in v0.48. The moustache of the man in the red shirt is named in 13 of his 22 pictures (none of 17 in v0.48, ten of 15 in v0.47): "A man with a moustache, in a red shirt and blue trousers". The beard of the man in green is named in none of his 25. Every animal is named for what it is: a dog in all 38 descriptions of a picture with one, a cat in all 10, the goat in all 5 and the duck in all 7, and one reader of the goat adds that its horns "could be read as ears". The older woman's glasses are named in all 21 of her descriptions. Against that, the grown figures are called young more often than in v0.48, not less. The woman in purple is a girl first in 9 of her 24 pictures (7 of 22), the woman in the yellow dress in 5 of 18 (1 of 18), the man in the red shirt a boy in 2 of 22 (2 of 17) and the man in green in 4 of 25 (1 of 24): "Girl, centre-front: dark ponytail, purple top, teal trousers; running to the right." The two counts are one screen each, of fourteen readers and of eleven; but a jaw was to make a grown figure read as grown, and it has not. The age bench had said so beforehand (`vision/isolation_v049.md`): figures of four casts, v0.48's, v0.49's and v0.49's with smaller heads, were called young equally often, and what the readers named when they were sure was grey hair, glasses, a cap or a moustache.

**What the full marks rest on.** The scorers listed 86 full marks as judgement calls, for 69 in v0.48's 87 pictures. In 42 the target stands beside another reading (33 in v0.48), and in 44 a near word or a target partly said was credited (36), twenty-three of them a word for a person's age. With the 42 halved, ten templates fall under 0.9 and 54 of the 64 pass: `dog_playing` (0.75, on four items), `play_catch` (0.812), `dog_sleeping`, `jump`, `rake` and `seesaw_heavy` (0.833), `balloon`, `blocked_hose`, `dog_begs` and `dog_wants_walk` (0.875). With all 86 halved, 43 pass, as in v0.48. The scorers gave five, nineteen, five, five and eight items under full marks, of 210, 231, 239, 212 and 252.

**Oddities and remarks.** The scorers logged 20 oddities in 19 of the 106 pictures, 0.2 a picture for v0.48's 0.4, and 4 of them in the set for 2. The readers' remarks were 2.32 a picture (2.38 in v0.48). The seesaw's and the slide's riders drew a remark in five pictures, for four: "she might be slightly floating above the seat, but it mostly reads as sitting". The figures in front of the pond drew one in three, each settled by the reader, and no description has a figure cut off at the picture's foot.
redrawn: `rain_coming` failed v0.48's gate and reads 1.00 in five pictures, one of its fifteen full marks a call; its drawing is v0.48's. `ice_cream`, the scoop at the mouth, reads 1.00 in fourteen pictures from 0.95 in twenty, with two calls about the eating for two half marks and eight. `goat_grazing`, its rope heavier, reads 1.00 in five pictures and the rope is named in all five. The templates of v0.48's list that were not worked carry the new heads: `lost_balloon` reads 0.972 in six pictures, on one half mark; `blocked_hose` 1.00 in five, where it had 0.95, with six of its twenty full marks a call; `about_to_trip` 1.00 in six; and `bird_steals` and `ducks_bread` 1.00, where they had 0.972 and 0.944. It is one screen, of 9 to 20 items a template, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.025 to 0.056: a template that went from a half mark to none has not been mended by a head. `play_catch` and `dog_begs` hold full marks by the gate and are under 0.9 on the strict count again.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (29 in three, 12 in four, 14 in five, 5 in six, 1 in seven, 1 in eight, 1 in fourteen and 1 in seventeen), and all 64 pass, where 63 did in v0.48 and in v0.47. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. One template is under 1.00, `lost_balloon` (0.972 on eighteen items in six pictures); the other 63 read 1.00, among them `rain_coming`, which failed the last gate, in five pictures. Per angle (`vision/v049/gate_yaw.json`), 19 of the 19 (template, angle) pairs pass, all at 1.00. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 42 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 54 of the 64 pass. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
calib: The new heads moved the calibration little: 24 of its 252 numbers moved by 0.002 or more and none by more than 0.014 (`cat_stalks_bird`'s inference, s from -0.482 to -0.496), and the planner's priors moved with them, by 0.01 or 0.02 for five templates. It was measured under the edge rule's second form, an animal's box 14 px clear of the picture's foot. The rule that stands, 8 px, came after it, when the tier-4 isomorph would not build. Of the 106 records built under 14 px, 104 rebuild to the pixel under 8 px, and `calibration.json` and the priors are left as measured.
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 46, and built three times, because the revision's edge rule was written three times (above). What is in the release is the third build, the second with two records built again. Thirteen cells have v0.48's seeds and templates. The tier-2 garden placed on its seed's second step with other templates. The tier-4 street placed by the free search after 14 seeds had failed, where v0.47 and v0.48 had built it from a forced set, and the walker about to trip is not in it. The tier-4 garden placed after 88 seeds of four searches had failed. The isomorphs are five: two of tier 2, two of tier 3 and one of tier 4, the last on v0.48's seed, third call. The probe pass built 62 and left nine templates short, each having lost its three groups to a partner (the storm beside a watering template, a second dog, the playground's events with each other); small forced groups added 16 and the pass stratified by angle 7: 85 probes, 51 gardens, 23 parks, 10 playgrounds and one street. **I looked at every picture of the second build on sheets before any reader had it, and built none again after that look for what it showed.** The three records built last, under the 8 px rule (the tier-2 garden, one angle probe and the tier-4 isomorph), I looked at only after the screen, and found nothing to mend. All 106 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 389 of 389. Its soft palette warning is raised by 332 records (283 of 352 in v0.48), with the median share of a figure's pixels on a palette colour as it was, 0.88. The target was not loosened.
